occurrences.source_excerpt: Centre of Mass (CM) = Centre of Gravity (CG) • CM: an object’s balance point • The body is composed of many parts. Each part can be considered as a single entity, and has a CG • The entire body can be considered as a single mass • S2 • The CG of the typical human body is located in the pelvic region, just anterior to S2 • The CG shifts as the component segments of the body change position or as weight is added or removed from the body

source_pages.source_file: 07 - 3. Analysis of Movement 運動動作分析.pdf
source_pages.formatted: 07 - 3. Analysis of Movement 運動動作分析.pdf, slide 15 (PDF p. 15)

occurrences.source_excerpt: Base of Support (BoS) • BoS • BoS: the contact area of an object with its supporting surface • A largerBoS allows the health worker to accomplish certain tasks with decreased force on the lower back • If the worker’s feet are close together (small BoS), even small weight shifts will move the body’s CG beyond the BoS, requiring the worker bend at the trunk to maintain balance, thus places a great deal of stress on the lower back muscles

source_pages.source_file: 07 - 3. Analysis of Movement 運動動作分析.pdf
source_pages.formatted: 07 - 3. Analysis of Movement 運動動作分析.pdf, slide 16 (PDF p. 16)

occurrences.source_excerpt: Stability v.s. Mobility Stability is promoted when: • The BoS is greater in area • BoS • The Line of Gravity (LoG) is near the center of BoS • The CG is lower & closer to the BoS Mobility is promoted when: • The BoS is smaller in area • The LoG is allowed to move • BoS beyond the center of the BoS • The distance of CG above the BoS • BoS is greater Remarks: The Line of Gravity (LoG) means the orientation & direction of gravity acting on the full body’s CoM

occurrences.source_excerpt: Patient position To achieve good body mechanics in the transfer task, the patient: • Moves forward in the chair, decreasing the distance between patient & caregiver • Place the feet under the CG and slightly apart to maximize the BoS BoS • Leans forward so that the LoG is as close as possible to the BoS • Places the hands on the armrests

occurrences.source_excerpt: Caregiver position • Toachieve good body mechanics in the transfer task, the caregiver: • Closes the distance between the caregiver and the patient by: • Bringing the feet into or close to the patient’s BoS • Flexing the trunk so that the caregiver is leaning slightly toward the patient

• e.g. forces generated by the muscles
